V. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE The Contractor shall provide to the U.S. Government the deliverables described in the Technical Specifications (Section I) of this Statement of Work. Further, the Contractor shall properly perform SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED 9 SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS all required testing, quality assurance, and validation on each Taskprior to submission for Government review. The final inspection and acceptance of ALL deliverables shall be performed by the U.S. Government upon completion and submission of the entire scope of work (Products 1 through 4). If INL Guatemala officials identify an incomplete, non- functional, or defective deliverable, they shall immediately refrain from accepting it and notify the Contractor in writing. Upon notification, the Contractor shall correct or replace the deficient deliverable at no additional cost to the Government. required for Task 3 (Production Deployment and User Acceptance Testing) and Task 4 (Knowledge Transfer). All coordination visits, deployment activities, and knowledge transfer sessions requiring physical presence shall take place at the GIO's institutional facilities in Guatemala City, Guatemala, as coordinated with the designated INL Guatemala point of contact. Remote work shall be permitted for all other tasks and activities where physical presence is not explicitly required, provided the Contractor maintains effective communication and coordination with INL Guatemala POC and the GIO throughout the period of performance. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP) This plan provides an effective method to promote satisfactory contractor performance. The QASP provides a method for the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to monitor Contractor performance, advise the Contractor of unsatisfactory performance, and notify the Contracting Officer of continued unsatisfactory performance. The Contractor, not the Government, is responsible for management and quality control to meet the terms of the contract. LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. Commissioning: Commissioning is a process that involves the entire Design Team throughout the planning, design, construction and occupancy of the project. Commissioning Guidelines for AOC Projects are contained in the policy statement of June 7, 2010. During the initial planning process, the AOC Project Team shall determine the purpose and role of commissioning. The purpose may be to ensure proper integration of a small renovation/rehabilitation into the Capitol 7 AOC Order 28-8, December 26, 2018 complex, or it may be related to a certification. It may range from simple, direct Owner commissioning by the AOC to an independent Commissioning Agent with a substantial budget. As a rule, if a project is designed by an Associate A/E, then commissioning will be performed by a third party hired by the AOC. Develop and document the Program of Requirements (PoR.) ii. Develop a basis of design. Commissioning shall help ensure that mechanical systems operate properly as a holistic system. The ARB is the official body providing design review for the Office of the Architect of the Capitol, but the Architect of the Capitol retains sole authority for final design approval. ARB review covers planning, design, appearance, and visibility of projects designed by consulting architects, in-house designers, and other parties. ARB review applies to third-party entities, not under contract to, or directly supervised by the Architect of the Capitol including, but not limited to, legislative branch agencies and public utilities. ip_data_security.text: nboarding the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) to the National Eye Institute’s (NEI) existing OpenSpecimen biobanking software instance and implementing associated Electronic Medical Record (EMR) integration services. Competition is restricted to Krishagni LLC because NHLBI’s requirement is specifically to onboard to NEI’s active, Krishagni-licensed and operated OpenSpecimen environment rather than to procure a separate standalone biobanking system. Acquiring a different biobanking product would not satisfy the requirement to join the existing NEI shared instance and would result in substantial duplication of software licensing, implementation, validation, and support infrastructure costs, as well as unacceptable operational delays. As the software developer, proprietor, and operator of the existing NEI OpenSpecimen environment, Krishagni LLC is the only responsible source authorized and technically capable of performing the required onboarding, workflow configuration, and EMR integration services within that shared platform.
